name: Nature View as Multi-Channel Prediction Confirmation
short_description: Window view of nature engages five convergent PE channels simultaneously: fractal fluency (T1), prospect/spatial depth (SC2), attention restoration (T25/ART), temporal variation (L5), ecological safety signal (T5/SRT); super-additive convergence explains consistent health benefits
higher_order_principle: Nature views produce convergent multi-channel prediction confirmation — the same structural principle that explains the power of daylight (L3) and natural materials (MAT4). The five channels (fractal fluency, prospect/spatial depth, attention restoration, temporal variation, ecological safety) each contribute independently; their simultaneous confirmation through a single stimulus (the nature view) produces a super-additive total. This is why nature views are the most consistently documented environmental contributor to wellbeing: they engage more convergent channels than any other single architectural element.

channel_1_fractal_fluency.mechanism: Natural scenes exhibit 1/f spatial frequency profiles with D ~ 1.3, matching visual system's processing structure

channel_2_prospect_spatial_depth.mechanism: Nature views provide spatial depth (long isovist) with vegetative partial enclosure — the prospect-refuge combination

channel_3_attention_restoration.mechanism: Natural scenes engage 'soft fascination' — involuntary attention to gently interesting stimuli permitting directed attention to rest

channel_4_temporal_variation.mechanism: Nature views are inherently dynamic: wind moves branches, clouds shift, light changes, seasons transform

channel_5_ecological_safety.mechanism: Green vegetation, water, spatial openness are evolutionary signals of resource-rich, safe environment

view_quality_gradient.HIGH: Biodiverse natural landscape with water, spatial depth, dynamic elements → all 5 channels → maximum convergence
view_quality_gradient.MODERATE: Managed nature (garden, park, tree canopy) → channels 1, 3, 4, 5; channel 2 partial → substantial convergence
view_quality_gradient.LOW: Sparse nature (single tree, lawn) → channels 1, 5 partial; 2, 3, 4 weak → modest convergence
view_quality_gradient.MINIMAL: Sky only → channel 4 only → minimal convergence (but still better than no view)
view_quality_gradient.NEGATIVE: Blank wall, parking lot, degraded environment → no channels; possible negative signal → no convergence

causal_links.evidence_base: Five-channel model is template synthesis; each channel independently supported (T1, SC2, T25, L5, T5)
Ulrich (1984, 1991); multiple replications across hospital, office, residential, prison settings
Kaplan (1995); multiple studies using backward digit span, ANT, sustained attention tasks
Heschong et al. (2002) — view content predicts student performance independently of illumination level

dose_response.threshold: 120 minutes per week of nature contact for significant health benefits
dose_response.architectural_implication: window views contribute continuous nature-contact minutes during daylight hours

scope_conditions: Applies to all buildings where windows or openings provide visual access to exterior environments
Benefit depends on view CONTENT — not all exterior views are restorative; degraded environments may produce negative effects
View benefits require ACTUAL visual access — photographs engage some channels (T1) but not others (temporal, depth, ecological safety at full strength)
Dose-response relationship suggests even partial nature views provide benefit, with diminishing returns at high exposure
moderators: view_quality (biodiverse landscape > garden > sparse > sky > built > wall)
window_properties (clear > tinted > frosted; larger area > smaller; lower sill > higher)
distance_to_nature (proximate for channels 1,5; distal for channel 2 prospect)
floor_level (upper floors provide wider prospect; ground floors closer nature contact)
season (deciduous varies; evergreen provides year-round channel engagement)
occupant_attention_state (depleted occupants benefit more from restoration)

synthetic_nature_hierarchy.note: Real nature outperforms synthetic because synthetic engages fewer channels
hierarchy: Real window view of nature (all 5 channels)

interactions.nature: T1 provides Channel 1 (fractal fluency). Nature views are the canonical T1 stimulus.
SC2 provides Channel 2 (prospect/spatial depth). Window view extends occupant's isovist beyond room boundary.
T25 provides Channel 3 (attention restoration). Nature views provide soft fascination for ART mechanism.
L5 provides Channel 4 (temporal variation). Nature views are inherently dynamic.
T5 provides Channel 5 (ecological safety). Nature views signal environmental safety, reducing HPA activation.
L3 is structural parallel: daylight engages 5+ channels. Window with daylight AND nature view provides BOTH convergences.
MAT4 is another parallel: wood engages 5 channels. VIEW1, L3, MAT4 establish multi-channel convergence as general principle.
VIEW1's five-channel convergence contributes to allostatic balance. Nature-view denial removes multi-channel contributor.
